# Reaction

`jaff.core.Reaction`

<!-- Generated by `python -m jaff._utils.api_docs`; do not edit. -->

A single astrochemical reaction with a symbolic rate expression.

## Constructor

`#!python Reaction(net, reactants, products, rate_coefficient, tmin, tmax, original_string, index, dE=None, t_cutoff='clip', type='unknown', photo=None, rad=None, format=None, metadata=None)`

**Parameters**

**net** : _Network_
: Network the reaction belongs to; supplies the auxiliary functions,
    radiation field, cross-section lookup and conservation-check mode.

**reactants** : _list[Specie]_
: Reactant species (may contain duplicates for three-body reactions).

**products** : _list[Specie]_
: Product species (may contain duplicates).

**rate_coefficient** : _Basic_
: SymPy expression for the rate coefficient.

**tmin** : _float or None_
: Lower temperature bound in Kelvin, or `None`.

**tmax** : _float or None_
: Upper temperature bound in Kelvin, or `None`.

**original_string** : _str_
: The raw network-file line that produced this reaction.

**index** : _int_
: File-side source number (`source_index`): the file-order row
    number of this reaction, gapped when rows merge.  Not an array
    subscript; see the `index` / `catalogue_index` attributes.

**dE** : _Expr or None, optional_
: Energy change per event (erg).  A `.jfunc` `deltae` function
    takes precedence; `None` (default) without one means zero.

**t_cutoff** : _str, optional_
: Out-of-range behaviour for the initial rate segment (`"clip"` by
    default); see the `t_cutoff` attribute.

**type** : _str, optional_
: Reaction type as concluded by the network-format parser (e.g.
    `"photo"`, `"cosmic_ray"`, `"3_body"`, `"unknown"`, or a
    grain surface-mechanism type).  Stored verbatim on the `type`
    attribute; defaults to `"unknown"`.

**photo** : _PhotoReactionProps or None, optional_
: Photo-reaction state; pass one for photo reactions, `None`
    (default) otherwise.

**rad** : _ReactionRadiationProps or None, optional_
: Emitted radiation.  `None` (default) builds one from the
    `.jfunc` `spectralYield` function, if any.

**format** : _str or None, optional_
: Name of the network-format parser that produced the reaction
    (e.g. `"prizmo"`); `None` (default) when unknown.

**metadata** : _dict or None, optional_
: Parser-private data attached at parse time; `None` (default)
    starts empty.

**Raises**

_SystemExit_
: When `net.spec.strict` is set and mass or charge is not conserved.

_ParserError_
: For invalid photo-reaction or shielding configuration.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reactants` | `Species` | Ordered species catalogue of reactant species. |
| `products` | `Species` | Ordered species catalogue of product species. |
| `rate_coefficient` | `Basic` | SymPy expression for the reaction rate coefficient (units depend on the reaction order; typically cm³ s⁻¹ for two-body reactions). Reassigning it refreshes `rate`. |
| `rate` | `Expr` | `rate_coefficient` times the core reactants' number densities, the reaction rate per unit volume used by every equation builder. |
| `tmin` | `float or None` | Minimum gas temperature at which the rate is valid (Kelvin). `None` means no lower bound. |
| `tmax` | `float or None` | Maximum gas temperature at which the rate is valid (Kelvin). `None` means no upper bound. |
| `t_cutoff` | `str` | Out-of-range behaviour for a piecewise (multi-segment) rate: `"clip"` holds the boundary value, otherwise the outermost segment extends unbounded. See `RateSegments`. |
| `rate_segments` | `RateSegments` | Per-temperature-range rate pieces. A single-range reaction holds one segment; reactions merged across disjoint ranges accumulate several, collapsed into `rate_coefficient` via `evaluate_equivalent_rate`. |
| `dE` | `Basic` | SymPy expression for the energy released per reaction event (erg). |
| `verbatim` | `str` | Human-readable string `"R1 + R2 -> P1 + P2"`. |
| `index` | `int` | File-side source number (`source_index`) of the reaction, i.e. its file-order row number. Stable per parsed row and gapped when rows merge (`duplicate_policy` or a temperature-range merge), so it is NOT a valid array subscript. Used for aux lookups (`chemRateN`) and `by_source_index`. |
| `catalogue_index` | `int` | Dense 0..count-1 position of this reaction in the parent `Reactions` catalogue, assigned by `add`. Safe to use as an array subscript in generated code. `-1` until catalogued. |
| `type` | `str` | Reaction type concluded by the parser and stored verbatim. Generic gas-phase values are `"photo"`, `"cosmic_ray"`, `"3_body"`, `"unknown"`; grain/ice networks add surface-mechanism types (see the module docstring for the full list). |
| `serialized` | `str` | Canonical form `"<sorted_reactants>__<sorted_products>"`. |
| `serialized_exploded` | `str` | Like `serialized` but built from the atom-level serialized forms of each species (isomer-insensitive comparison). |
| `photo` | `PhotoReactionProps or None` | Photo-reaction state, `None` for non-photo reactions: `xsec` (cross sections of the single decay channel, an `XsecProps`), `pi_database` (per-reaction photoionization database override), `custom_rad_rate` (rate supplied by a `.jfunc` aux function), `rgrouped` (per-band data; see `band_xsecs`) and `shielding`; the spectrum-averaged cross section is `xsec.total` (cm²). |
| `rad` | `ReactionRadiationProps` | Radiation the reaction emits: `spectral_yield` (from a `.jfunc` `spectralYield` function, or `None`) and its per-group integrals `group_yields` (set when a radiation field is configured). |

## Properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`rate_coefficient`](rate_coefficient.md) | SymPy rate coefficient; see the class attributes. |
| [`rate`](rate.md) | Reaction rate per unit volume, `rate_coefficient · Π nden[reactants]`. |
| [`species`](species.md) | All unique species involved in this reaction (reactants ∪ products). |
| [`elements`](elements.md) | All elements present across reactants and products. |
| [`band_xsecs`](band_xsecs.md) | Band-averaged cross sections for this reaction, one row per band. |
